what_happened: check-metalogic-cycles.sh's ALLOWLIST comment (line 199) still says 8 lines from one source, but the frozen set as landed is 10 lines from two sources (_SRC: 8, _SRC_OPEN: 2) per the script's own header at line 37. The dispatch's item 5 text cited an 8-line figure; the guidance must not restate that stale count -- describe the allowlist structurally (equality not containment, frozen explicit pairs) rather than with a number that already drifted once.

Resolved item 2's open siting question (dispatch 'the one open question the implementer should resolve in research'): core's plan-format.md (lines ~357-435) already documents verify-deploy.sh's target-shape contract in detail, including the exact failure mode (an extension source_dir lacks .claude/, so gate0 exits 2), so item 2's positive-form fact is largely already core-documented. The genuinely new content for the lean-extension guidance is the pre-existing-findings corollary (a red gate whose findings are pre-existing and out-of-scope is a pass, not a blocker) phrased for a plan author writing an ad hoc criterion -- that framing does not already exist in core's generic plan-authoring material (core's own pre-existing/baseline language is scoped to the orchestrator's internal batch-deploy mechanism, not to a plan author's own gate criteria). Recommendation: keep item 2 in the lean extension's new file as approved, state the target-shape fact tersely with a pointer to plan-format.md's authoritative sub-case (b) treatment rather than re-deriving it, and treat the pre-existing-findings corollary as the new content.

Planning needed no independent investigation: the research report had already fixed the target path (externally constrained by task 840's dependency), resolved the item 2 siting question as reference-rather-than-duplicate, and flagged one stale dispatch figure (the '8-line' allowlist count) to omit. The only fresh check the plan phase ran was confirming /home/benjamin/.config/nvim holds both a deployed .claude/ tree and agent-system/extensions, so the gate-3,4 narrowing invocation named in two phases' Tier Justification lines is actually meetable -- itself an instance of the item 2 lesson the plan is about.

The dispatch numbers two different items '4': the absolute-vs-baseline-delta class in the original block (acceptance criteria 11-12 refer to it) and typst-sync-check.sh Check 2 in the ADDED ITEMS 4-9 addendum. The plan resolves this by giving the guidance file its own sequential numbering of nine conditions, folding the addendum's item 4 into condition 1 as a second trigger condition on one surface (which the dispatch itself directs) and keeping absolute-vs-delta as condition 4. No content is lost, but a reader comparing the plan's condition numbers to the dispatch's item numbers will not find a one-to-one match for the addendum items.

Phase 1's own Condition 4 rule (baseline delta, not absolute zero) was immediately exercised: the gate-3 doc-lint run against the nvim config root returned two pre-existing findings unrelated to the new file, correctly recorded as baseline rather than a blocker.
